chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ayyub ibn Sulaym al-Attar, from Ishaq ibn Bishr al-Kahili, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said:
Whoever enters the market, buys a gift, and brings it to his family is like one who carries charity to a needy people. And let him begin with the daughters before the sons,

for whoever gladdens a daughter, it is as if he freed a slave from the Children of Ismail. And whoever gladdens the eye of a son, it is as if he wept out of awe before God, the Mighty and Majestic. And whoever weeps out of awe before God, the Mighty and Majestic, God will enter him into the Gardens of Bliss.

key_terms.تحفة: Gift, present — specifically a thoughtful item brought from the market
key_terms.جنات النعيم: Gardens of Bliss — a description of Paradise in the Quran
key_terms.خشية الله: Awe and reverential fear of God — distinct from worldly fear, denoting spiritual consciousness
key_terms.رقبة: Literally 'neck', idiomatically refers to freeing a slave — a major virtuous act in Islamic tradition
key_terms.محاويج: Those in need, the needy — plural of muhtaj

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Muhammad say about bringing gifts to your family from the marketplace?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) encouraged bringing gifts home from the marketplace, comparing the act to giving charity to the needy. He specifically instructed to prioritize daughters before sons, offering extraordinary spiritual rewards: gladdening a daughter is likened to freeing a slave from the descendants of Prophet Ismail, while gladdening a son is likened to weeping out of divine awe, which itself leads to paradise. This hadith was delivered in a pre-Islamic Arabian context where daughters were often undervalued, and the Prophet's emphatic prioritizing of daughters represents a direct corrective to that cultural norm.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-`Attar (ra) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us from Salama b. al-Khattab from Ayyub b. Sulaym al-`Attar from Ishaq b. Bishr al-Kahili from Salim al-Aftas from Sa`id b. Jubayr from Ibn `Abbas. He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said:
He who enters the market, buys a gift, and brings it to his family is like one who brings charity to a needy people. He should start with the females before the males,

for he who gladdens his daughter is like one who frees a slave from the Children of Isma`il. He who gladdens the eye of his son is like one who weeps out of humility before Allah; and whoever weeps out of humility before Allah, Allah will enter him into the Paradise of Bliss.
